title: Nouns: gender, articles and plurals
summary: Every noun is masculine or feminine; articles and plurals follow.
focus: Noun gender, el/la/un/una, plural formation, al and del
content:
## Every noun has a gender

Spanish nouns are **masculine** or **feminine**, even for objects. The ending is a strong clue.

| usually masculine | usually feminine |
|---|---|
| **-o**: el libro, el chico | **-a**: la casa, la chica |
| **-or**: el profesor | **-ción / -sión**: la canción, la televisión |
| **-ma** (Greek origin): el problema, el idioma | **-dad / -tad**: la ciudad, la universidad |
| days, months, numbers: el lunes, el tres | letters of the alphabet: la a, la be |

Common exceptions to learn as words: **la mano** (hand), **el día** (day), **la foto**, **la moto**.

## The articles

| | masculine | feminine |
|---|---|---|
| the (singular) | **el** | **la** |
| the (plural) | **los** | **las** |
| a / an | **un** | **una** |
| some, a few | **unos** | **unas** |

- *el coche, la mesa, un amigo, una amiga, unos libros, unas chicas*

## Al and del

When **a** or **de** meets **el**, they fuse: **a + el = al**, **de + el = del**.

- *Voy **al** cine.*: I'm going to the cinema.
- *El libro **del** profesor.*: The teacher's book.

This never happens with *la, los, las*: *a la playa, de los niños*.

## Making plurals

1. Ends in a **vowel** → add **-s**: casa → casas, coche → coches.
2. Ends in a **consonant** → add **-es**: ciudad → ciudades, profesor → profesores.
3. Ends in **-z** → change to **-ces**: lápiz → lápices, vez → veces.

Nouns ending in **-s** with an unstressed last syllable do not change: *el lunes → los lunes*.

A masculine plural can cover a mixed group: *los padres* = the parents, *los hijos* = the children (sons and daughters).

vocabulary.example: El libro está en la mesa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The book is on the table.

quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in -ción are feminine: la canción.
Nouns ending in -ma of Greek origin are masculine: el problema, el idioma.

quiz.prompt: Complete: la mochila ___ profesor (the teacher's backpack)

quiz.explanation: Mano is one of the exceptions: it ends in -o but is feminine.
Casa is feminine, so 'some houses' is unas casas: article and noun both plural.
Día ends in -a but is masculine: el día, buenos días.

listening.note: Problema ends in -ma but is masculine.

listening.text: La casa del profesor es pequeña.
Los coches están en la calle.
listening.meaning: The cars are in the street.
listening.note: New word: la calle = the street.

listening.text: Las chicas cantan una canción todos los días.
listening.meaning: The girls sing a song every day.

listening.text: El chico tiene un lápiz en la mano.
listening.meaning: The boy has a pencil in his hand.
listening.note: La mano is feminine despite the -o.

listening.text: Las ventanas de la casa son muy grandes.
listening.meaning: The windows of the house are very big.
listening.note: New word: la ventana = the window.

listening.text: Los chicos de la clase tienen unos libros y unos lápices nuevos.
listening.meaning: The boys in the class have some new books and pencils.
listening.note: Lápiz ends in -z, so the plural is lápices.

conversations.title: At the stationery shop
conversations.scenario: Pablo buys school things from the shop assistant.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buenas tardes. Necesito unos lápices y un cuaderno.
lines.meaning: Good afternoon. I need some pencils and a notebook.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro. ¿Los lápices del paquete grande o del pequeño?
lines.meaning: Of course. The pencils from the big pack or the small one?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Del pequeño. Y una mochila para los libros.
lines.meaning: From the small one. And a backpack for the books.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tenemos unas mochilas muy bonitas. ¿La roja o la azul?
lines.meaning: We have some very nice backpacks. The red one or the blue one?

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: The blue one, please. How much is it?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No, gracias. Voy al colegio ahora.
lines.meaning: No, thanks. I'm going to the school now.

bites.title: Endings give it away
bites.rule: Words in -o, -or and Greek -ma are usually el; words in -a, -ción and -dad are usually la. Check the ending first.
bites.example: el libro, el problema, la canción, la ciudad
bites.example_meaning: the book, the problem, the song, the city

bites.title: The exceptions
bites.rule: La mano and la foto end in -o but are feminine; el día ends in -a but is masculine. Learn each one together with its article.
bites.example_meaning: Good morning. I have two hands.

bites.title: Plurals: s, es, ces
bites.rule: Vowel? Add -s. Consonant? Add -es. Ends in -z? Change it to -ces.
bites.example: casa → casas, ciudad → ciudades, lápiz → lápices

bites.title: a + el = al, de + el = del
bites.rule: A and de fuse with el into al and del. They never fuse with la, los or las.
bites.example: Voy al cine. El libro del profesor.
bites.example_meaning: I'm going to the cinema. The teacher's book.

sorts.title: El or la?
sorts.why: -o, -or and -ma usually take el; -a, -ción and -dad usually take la, except for words like la mano and el día.

sorts.title: How does the plural end?
sorts.why: Vowel endings add -s, consonants add -es, and -z changes to -ces.

sorts.title: Fuse or not?
buckets: a la / de la / de los
sorts.why: Only el fuses: a + el = al, de + el = del.

spots.why: Problema is a Greek -ma word, so it's masculine: un problema.
Nouns ending in -z change to -ces in the plural.
Nouns in -ción are feminine: la canción.
Mesa is feminine, so 'some' is unas.

spots.sentence: Tengo un libro en el mano.
spots.why: Mano ends in -o but is feminine: la mano.
Ciudad ends in a consonant, so add -es.

builds.text: Necesito unos lápices y un cuaderno.
builds.meaning: I need some pencils and a notebook.
